description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The FTF Bangladesh Nutrition activity improves nutrition outcomes of children under five, pregnant and lactating women, and adolescent girls. The activity's technical assistance and social and behavioral communication interventions will increase access to nutritious, diverse, and safe diets; strengthen social and economic empowerment; and improve adoption of good water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) practices by rural households. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will facilitate private and public sector partners to train service providers, market actors, rural households, and other critical stakeholders. These training will build the knowledge and skills needed to increase the demand and supply of nutritious, diverse, and safe foods, which will lead to increased dietary diversity. The activity will continue to empower women and adolescents to engage in economic activities, adopt healthy behaviors, and participate in household decision-making. The activity will work with private companies and local entrepreneurs to create awareness in rural households and to offer improved sanitation, safe drinking water, and hygiene solutions. The activity will support the Global Food Security Strategy and the Multisectoral Nutrition Strategy by incorporating nutrition-sensitive interventions that empower women, target poorer households, and engage public and private sector partners.The activity aligns with the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan goal two and Integrated Country Strategy MO 3.2 Improved food and water security and air quality. Funding for this activity contributes to the Global Food Security ($5.8m), Water ($2m), Gender Equality/Women's Empowerment - Secondary ($800k), GBV ($900k), GBV-CEFM($700k), Private Sector Engagement ($800k), MSME($1.5M) earmarks and directives.
